reason: Compute Hilb_R from the monomial basis of the weighted polynomial ring. Then quotient successively by the homogeneous regular sequence: at each step the non-zero-divisor property gives a degreewise exact sequence, so the Hilbert series is multiplied by 1 - q^(r+s). This yields the stated product formula. Since the coefficients are dimensions of graded pieces, they are nonnegative integers, and boundedness of the resulting series as q approaches 1 from below forces only finitely many nonzero graded pieces, so A is finite-dimensional.
